Subject: DPA redlines / no-train and prompt ownership questions

Tessa —

Thanks for sending the draft DPA. Two high-level asks from our side as we prepare redlines:

1) No-training commitment: we need an explicit, contractual no-training ("no-model-improvement") clause that covers our tenant data and prompt/response pairs. Beyond the clause, we will need operational evidence showing separation of data paths (logs, KV caching, any telemetry), plus an attestation that production traffic is not used for model updates.

2) Prompt/response ownership: we need language confirming that TheraTech retains IP in prompts and generated responses for our tenant, and we need to understand any retained logs that might contain PII or derivative outputs.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: please provide the current subprocessor inventory and confirm how cross-border routing is controlled (we have EU customers and want to avoid transfers to non-EU jurisdictions unless SCCs or equivalent controls are in place).

Attached is our first-pass redline (TheraTech_DPA_redline_v1.pdf). Can you confirm what evidence Redwood can provide operationally (diagrams, logs, attestation, runbooks) and an approximate timeline for providing those artifacts?

If helpful, Ethan (cc'd) can share a checklist of the specific evidence categories their procurement counsel expects.

Best,
Sofia Rinaldi
Head of Legal Ops, TheraTech

Sofia / Ethan —

Thanks for the patience. Per our internal run (notes summarized below) — we are prepared to deliver the evidence pack and a proposed DPA paragraph for the no-training / prompt/response ownership items. Deliverables (attached): Operational_Evidence_Plan_v1.pdf (contains architecture diagram, subprocessor CSV link, sample audit extract, attestation template, and runbook excerpt).

Key points to confirm in the DPA redline:
• No-training commitment: Redwood will not use customer tenant prompts or generated responses to improve or retrain any models used for customer inference, excepting a tightly-scoped telemetry set described in the runbook (aggregated usage metrics and sanitized diagnostic telemetry). The DPA will list the allowed telemetry categories.

• Prompt/response ownership: TheraTech retains IP in prompts and generated outputs. Redwood will retain ephemeral logs for operational purposes only and will provide retention windows; any retained artifacts will be encrypted at rest and subject to the retention policy in the DPA.

• Subprocessors & transfers: Redwood will provide an up-to-date subprocessor inventory and will mark each processor's region. For EU data, Redwood will enable EU-hosted inference and offer SCCs (or equivalent) and onshore KMS where required.

Constraints and clarifications:
- We cannot provide model weight snapshots or proprietary training artifacts.
- The evidence pack will include sample scrubbed logs and the signed attestation from David's team; the attestation will be suitable for procurement review.

Next steps:
1) Ethan — can you confirm the secure URL (SFTP or Drive) where you want the artifact pack?
2) Sofia — we'll push a suggested DPA paragraph (track-change) within the next 24 hours for your counsel to review.
3) Marissa — follow up with procurement to align on contract milestone for signature.

Thanks — happy to set a short (30 min) call Monday if you prefer to walk the pack together.

Tessa Morgan
VP, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
